chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, who said:

I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man does not become a worshipper until he becomes forbearing, and indeed, among the Children of Israel, a man was not counted as a worshipper until he remained silent for ten years prior to that.'

key_terms.حَلِيماً: forbearing (one who is gentle, patient, and composed)

ai.seo_question: What is the prerequisite for a person to be considered a true worshipper according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) establishes that true worship (ibadah) is contingent upon possessing the quality of forbearance (hilm), illustrating this by citing the practice of the Children of Israel, where a person was not considered a true worshipper until they had practiced silence for ten years. This highlights that inner composure and restraint are prerequisites for valid devotion, a concept deeply rooted in Shia hadith literature as a bridge between ritual piety and moral character. The emphasis on silence serves as a disciplinary mechanism to purify the tongue and heart before engaging in higher forms of spiritual service.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Muhammad Bin Ubeydullah who said,

‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The man cannot become a worshipper until he becomes forbearing, and it was so among the Children of Israel, that a worshipper was not counted as a worshipper until he was silent for ten years before that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd Allah who has said the following: “I heard al-Rida (a.s.) saying, ‘A man cannot become a worshipper until he becomes a forbearing one. A man in the tribe of Israel wanting to become a worshipper had to keep silent for ten years before he could be considered a worshipper.’”
